study.title: Effectiveness and cerebral responses of multi-points acupuncture for primary insomnia: a preliminary randomized clinical trial and fMRI study
study.article_type: randomized controlled trial with neuroimaging substudy
study.study_design: patient-assessor-blinded, randomized and sham controlled trial
study.randomization: randomized via network system of Clinical Evaluation Center of China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences
study.population: PI patients recruited from outpatient clinics in the Neurological Department of China-Japan Union Hospital of Jilin University and Changchun University of Chinese Medicine
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) patients who were over 18 years old, but under 65 years old; (2) patients who had no problems with communication and intelligence; (3) patients with a wake after sleep onset (WASO) or sleep onset latency (SOL) of > 30 min for at least 3 nights every week, and symptoms lasting for over 3 months; (3) patients with an AIS score of ≥6; (4) patients with a PSQI score of > 7
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) patients with uncontrolled medical conditions suspected to interfere with sleep; (2) patients with uncontrolled psychiatric conditions requiring immediate treatment; (3) patients diagnosed of comorbid sleep disorders; (4) patients with a self-rating depression scale (SDS) or self-rating anxiety scale (SAS) of ≥50; (5) patients with alcohol and/or other drug abuse or dependence; (6) Pregnant or nursing patients, or those of childbearing age who have not adopted appropriate birth control methods; (7) patients with who took hypnotic or sedating medications, or accepted acupuncture treatment in the recent 1 month

extraction_notes.note: Adverse events results are not explicitly reported as counts or outcomes; the paper only describes the monitoring procedure. It is unclear whether any adverse events occurred.

Blinding success, credibility, and expectancy were not formally assessed or reported as outcome measures. Only the MASS sensory scale was used to verify De-Qi; no patient-level allocation guessing or credibility instrument was reported.
The paper does not report n_completed per arm separately; it only states 129 patients were included in the final analysis divided equally (43 per group). Dropout details are not provided.

The sham (N-Acu) group received needle insertion at a non-acupoint location WITH electrical stimulation at the same parameters (4 Hz, De-Qi intensity) as the verum groups. This means the sham procedure involved genuine penetration and electrical stimulation, differing from verum only in acupoint location. This should be flagged for sham classification.

For the PSG R (REM) outcome, the paper states P = 0.001 for S-Acu group within-group change, while for M-Acu it states P = 0.017. These are reported differently in text vs. Table 4 footnotes (Table 4 footnote marks S-Acu R as 'a' = P < 0.01, and M-Acu R as 'b' = P < 0.05). Used table values for extraction.

The paper describes TST post-treatment for S-Acu as '288.25 ± 76.51' with footnote 'b' (P < 0.05 compared with baseline), while the text states 'TST (P = 0.020)'. These are consistent and preserved as reported.

The fMRI subsample selection was stratified by age groups (18-35, 36-50, 51-65) with 5 randomly selected per stratum per arm. The exact demographic breakdown of the neuroimaging subsample is not separately reported.

Table 6 (AIS correlation analysis) lists two rows for Middle Temporal Gyrus in the left hemisphere with overlapping labels. The first row (cluster size 34, t=-6.25, MNI -57,-57,-3) appears to be a separate smaller cluster from the second row (cluster size 217, t=-7.53, MNI -57,-42,0) which also includes Superior Temporal Gyrus. Both were extracted as separate coordinate rows.
The paper does not report whether the neuroimaging subsample analysis was pre-specified or exploratory, nor does it report separate demographic statistics for the fMRI subsample.
No between-group comparison of TST increase is formally reported for S-Acu vs N-Acu or M-Acu vs N-Acu in Table 5. Table 5 only compares S-Acu and M-Acu groups.

The paper uses 'FWE correct P = 0.05' as the cluster-level correction threshold throughout neuroimaging analyses. The voxel-level threshold varies: P < 0.001 for the correlation and ANOVA analyses, and P < 0.005 for the post-hoc between-group comparisons. These were extracted exactly as reported per analysis.
The FOV for the rs-fMRI is reported as '106 × 106 × 46' which appears to be the matrix/slice dimensions rather than a standard FOV in mm. This was transcribed exactly as reported.
